task: Escribe un anuncio de 70–90 palabras para buscar un compañero de tándem: quién eres, qué idioma ofreces y buscas, tus temas favoritos y cuándo puedes reunirte.
paragraphs: For years I studied English at school, but I could hardly hold a conversation. I knew the rules, I had done hundreds of exercises, and yet, when a tourist asked me for directions, my mind went blank.

Everything changed when a friend told me about language exchanges, also called tandems. The idea is simple: two people who want to learn each other's language meet regularly and spend half of the time speaking one language and half speaking the other. There are no teachers and no exams. You just talk.

My partner was Owen, a Welsh engineer who had just moved to my city and wanted to improve his Spanish. We met every Thursday in a café near the station. At first, it was awkward. I spoke slowly and kept apologising for my mistakes. Owen did the same in Spanish. After a few weeks, though, we stopped worrying and started laughing at our errors.

We agreed on a few rules. We corrected each other only when a mistake made the message unclear, or when the other person asked. Each of us brought a topic to discuss, from football to politics. And we always wrote down three new expressions in a notebook.

In six months, my English improved more than in six years at school. I learned phrases that are never in textbooks, like "I'm knackered" (I'm very tired) or "it's not my cup of tea". More importantly, I lost my fear of speaking.

Owen went back to Wales two years ago, but we still talk online every month. Last summer I visited him in Cardiff, and he introduced me to his family as "my teacher". I told them the truth: we taught each other.
